segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
drive in a lane that is not adjacent to the lane in which the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency is moving,
unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, not an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach (rel.centre_distance; no clearance read). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move', as defined in s10: visible from the subject (rel.visible) with an arm signal (sig.hand_signal other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix the lights: a lamp lit of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); exclusions are the reading's. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle. 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer; excepted where such a device governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'drive in a lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies; st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'), the lane being the subject's own feature; 'the lane in which the ... vehicle ... is moving' is a lane the approached vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane). 'adjacent' is read in two ways the contracts carry: the left or right neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; not the marking between the lanes), and, for a vehicle moving against the subject's direction, the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions — each of lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'), their designated directions opposed (st.lane_direction) — on one and the same roadway that both road users occupy (st.roadway, 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate', so a divided highway's opposing lanes are never adjacent). A lane is not adjacent to itself.

The section's definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: visible from the subject (rel.visible); '(a) A movement of the vehicle' kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator). 'about to move' is read through these indications.

operationalizations.convention: lane-change time: moving away from the vehicle's lane is possible once the approach has lasted the time a driver needs to perceive the vehicle and change one lane, and only where the subject's way carries a candidate lane: a lane on the same highway as the subject's lane (st.on_way) whose designated direction points the subject's way (st.lane_direction, positive dot product with the subject's lane direction) and that is not adjacent to the vehicle's lane

operationalizations.standard: unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance and lane availability: a candidate lane is impossible (roadway) where a temporary traffic control device governs it, and unsafe (traffic) where a road user occupying it, other than the subject (any road user using the highway: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances', DEF-NRS-484A-285, read without exclusion), is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface (ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry); weather makes the move unsafe where the road is icy or snow-covered, or the visibility (env.visibility) is shorter than the distance the subject travels at its speed in the lane-change time

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp red, flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject and e's sig.hand_signal other than no_signal or sig.turn_indicator other than off); e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
obligation: For every e selected as in the applicability for which that whole selection has held at every observation of the window behind of length p.emergency_lane_change_window, every st.lane Le that e occupies and every st.lane Ls that the subject occupies: Ls is not adjacent to Le, or the move is excused. Adjacent: Ls is the left or right neighbour of Le (st.lane_adjacency), or Ls and Le each have lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal) with designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose dot product is negative while some st.roadway is occupied (rel.occupies) by both the subject and e. Excused where env.ice_or_snow holds; or env.visibility is below the subject's kin.speed × p.emergency_lane_change_window; or no candidate lane is open and clear. A candidate lane C is a st.lane lying on (st.on_way) the same st.highway as Ls, whose designated direction has a positive dot product with Ls's, and which is not adjacent to Le in the sense above; C is open and clear where no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs) and no road user u other than the subject occupying C has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move', defined as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is read through the visible indications the definition lists and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible)

the catch-all 'other conditions' is read only through the contracts named: a closure by temporary traffic control, the gap to traffic occupying the candidate lane, ice or snow, a wet surface or precipitation, and visibility

adjacency across the centre of a two-way roadway is read only between the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions on one roadway; the vehicle's own lane is not adjacent to itself, so following it in its lane is not read as a breach of this paragraph

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road, four lanes in the subject's direction. A police car (authorized emergency vehicle) with its red front lamp flashing moves in lane 1 ahead of the subject; the subject has been approaching it within the reach for longer than the lane-change window and stays in lane 2, the neighbour of lane 1, while lanes 3 and 4 are open and empty.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject has moved to lane 3, which is not a neighbour of lane 1.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives in lane 2 of a four-lane carriageway; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe lane adjacency, so whether the subject's lane neighbours the police car's lane, and which lanes are candidates, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Two lanes in the subject's direction; the police car moves in lane 1 and the subject in lane 2. The only lane not adjacent to lane 1 is lane 1 itself, occupied by the police car within the headway gap, so no candidate lane is clear: excused.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the road is covered in snow (env.ice_or_snow): excused.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the approach has lasted less than the lane-change window when the subject is observed in lane 2.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Undivided two-way roadway, two lanes each way. A regulatory-agency official vehicle with its red front lamp flashing moves against the subject in the leftmost lane of its direction; the subject, approaching it head-on, drives in the leftmost lane of its own direction, while the right lane of its direction is open and empty.

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: warning-lamp conspicuity and perception-reaction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_267_2a)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_lane_change_window
param_proposals.convention: the time from the onset of an approach to an emergency or enforcement vehicle until a driver has moved one lane over: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one lane change of about 4 s
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_dry
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_wet
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_ice
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)
